decisions.executionNote: Begin mirrored elbow-up lift and wrist reorientation with half-size increments; then visually target yellow and purple nuts in their own workspaces.
Move above yellow nut with left and purple nut with right, completing vertical approach orientation. Heights and centers are estimated from calibrated head RGB.
Refine nut centers using wrist views and corrected tabletop height, then lower open grippers to grasp height without crossing workspaces.
Center each nut between the fingers from wrist RGB, close fully, and lift vertically to check retention before moving to matching screws.
Both nuts remain visible between fingers after lifting. Carry yellow and purple above their matching screws with closed grippers and vertical axes; refine placement from the next wrist views.
Correct the small rightward screw-axis offsets in both wrist views and lower held nuts toward thread engagement height, slowing near the screws.
Fine-center the visible screw tips within the nut holes, then begin a slow clockwise engagement turn with slight descent; monitor for lateral displacement.
Continue a controlled clockwise turn on both aligned pairs with slight axial descent, preserving elbow-up configuration and closed grasp.
Release and reset wrists for another tightening stroke. Yellow showed lateral resistance, so pause axial advance and reassess its alignment after release.
Purple remains seated after release; regrasp and tighten it. Yellow came off the screw, so move the left hand safely above the displaced nut for recovery.
Lower the open left gripper toward the recovered yellow nut for a fresh centered grasp; continue the seated purple nut's clockwise stroke with minimal axial advance.
Refine the left nut's lateral and fore-aft centering while descending to grasp height. Release the purple nut and reset the right wrist for the next clockwise stroke.
Close on the centered yellow nut and lift for retention check. Regrasp purple and apply another controlled clockwise tightening segment with minimal descent.
Carry the retained yellow nut back above its screw with added clearance. Finish the current purple tightening stroke and release to inspect whether the pair stays seated.
Lower the newly centered yellow nut to engagement height without turning yet. Reset the released right wrist while leaving the purple pair undisturbed.
Yellow now appears centered over its screw; turn clockwise with almost no axial forcing. Apply one more controlled tightening stroke to purple after regrasping.
Release both nuts and reset wrists. Retract right vertically to inspect the purple pair; keep left near yellow to verify whether it stayed on the screw or needs re-centering.
Purple remains assembled after release and retraction. Yellow fell beside its screw; approach its newly observed center with clearance, aiming for a more centered grasp.

The open right finger appears close to the yellow screw and descent lagged. Narrow the empty left gripper, restore vertical orientation, and approach the nut more slowly with separation from the screw.
Center the yellow nut fore-aft and laterally between the narrowed fingers, close, and lift slightly to verify a stable centered grasp. Keep the released purple pair clear.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Lift yellow clear and move above its screw with the right hand stationary.
Yellow nut and screw now appear laterally aligned. Descend vertically without turning to inspect the initial seating geometry.
The yellow screw tip is centered but still shallow in the nut. Advance slowly while turning clockwise, checking for actual seating rather than assuming rotation alone engaged it.
Corrected the invalid tensor; no motion occurred. Relieve yellow contact, shift toward its screw axis based on the rotated wrist view, and reapproach without turning.
Refine the remaining small yellow screw-axis offset visible through the bore, with a slow axial approach and no added torque until aligned.
Yellow screw tip is now centered within the bore. Apply a slow clockwise threading stroke with only 1.5 mm of axial advance, checking that the nut remains upright.
Yellow shows an off-axis crescent after rotation, suggesting an eccentric grasp. Translate toward the visible screw axis without further turning, and lower only 2 mm to inspect seating.
Corrected rejected tensor; no prior movement occurred. Make the remaining lateral correction, settle yellow straight down, and release to inspect whether it stays on its screw.
Yellow stayed upright and settled around its screw after release. Raise slightly and reset the open wrist for a centered tightening grasp; leave purple undisturbed.
Re-center the left gripper on the settled yellow nut rather than the previous eccentric grasp, then close and start a controlled clockwise tightening stroke.
Yellow is now upright with the screw tip centered and flush in its bore. Finish this tightening stroke, release, and lift slightly to inspect stability before addressing blue.
Yellow and purple remain assembled after release. Raise left clear, reset its wrist, and approach above the blue nut in the left workspace.
Use the blue nut's head and wrist locations to correct its approach center, restore a vertical gripper axis, and descend open to just above grasp height.
Blue is laterally centered. Lower the final 15 mm with the gripper open, then inspect fore-aft centering at grasp height before closing.
Make a small final centering correction for blue, close the left gripper, and lift vertically to verify retention before transport.
Blue remains in the closed gripper after lifting. Raise for clearance and carry it above its matching screw, staying entirely in the left workspace.
Align blue's small lateral offset and descend vertically toward engagement height without twisting, using the centered grasp to avoid the earlier yellow eccentricity.
The near-field view shows blue's screw tip offset to the right. Correct that offset before turning and approach the thread entrance slowly.
Make the final small blue-axis correction, lower straight to seat it, and release so the nut can settle concentrically before a centered tightening grasp.
Lift left slightly and allow the released blue nut to settle for inspection; its axis may still be tilted. Begin the right arm's elbow-up retreat toward home, clear of purple.
Re-center on the settled blue nut and close for an upright tightening grasp, without twisting yet. Continue the right arm's smooth elbow-up return.
Apply a controlled clockwise stroke to blue with minimal axial advance. Finish the right arm's gradual return to its observed home pose, keeping its gripper open.
Blue now appears upright and concentric with its screw. Release fully before lifting and resetting the left wrist, then inspect that all three pairs remain together.
All three pairs remain together after releasing blue. Begin a clear, elbow-up left-arm retreat toward origin while refining the right home pose; keep both grippers open.
Complete the left arm's continuous elbow-up return to its initial pose, with both grippers open and all assembled pairs left untouched.
Settle both open grippers precisely at their starting poses and inspect the three released assemblies without further contact.
Hold both arms at origin with open grippers while checking that the three released matching assemblies remain stable.
Purple's bore still looks deeper than the other two assemblies. Reapproach with the right arm for a closer check and, if needed, another tightening stroke; keep left home.
Complete the right arm's vertical approach above the purple assembly, retaining clearance before a centered regrasp.
Lower the open right gripper toward purple's nut, correcting its small lateral offset and keeping the approach vertical for a centered tightening grasp.
Purple is centered at grasp height but its screw tip is still recessed. Close the right gripper, settle slightly, and apply a clockwise tightening segment; keep left at origin.
Continue purple's clockwise tightening with a small axial advance, then release at the end of the stroke to inspect its seating depth.
Purple remains seated but still recessed. Reset the fully open right wrist with slight clearance so the next grasp can be centered lower on the nut rather than its upper edge.
Approach lower on the seated purple nut with a small fore-aft centering adjustment, then close without rotating to verify a secure grasp at the new depth.
Turn the securely regrasped purple nut clockwise while following it downward gradually. Inspect whether the screw tip becomes less recessed; keep left open at origin.
Release purple fully to let it settle without lateral load, then reset the open right wrist at the current height. Inspect seating before applying further axial motion.
Re-center the right grip fore-aft on purple's nut, close without lifting the assembly, and test a short clockwise stroke with minimal axial advance.
Continue purple's clockwise turn while following the nut downward slowly. Its screw tip remains recessed; watch for seating or resistance rather than relying on commanded rotation.

Purple appears increasingly off-center relative to the gripping fingers. Release and lift with an open-wrist reset to remove lateral load and inspect its actual settled axis before further tightening.
Regrasp the settled purple nut at its observed center with a corrected vertical orientation. Descend without twisting, then close and inspect the grasp before another stroke.
Apply a final controlled clockwise stroke from the centered purple regrasp, with only 1 mm axial advance and no lateral motion, then inspect after release.
Release purple fully before retracting and resetting the empty right wrist. Inspect the settled assembly without further lateral loading; keep left at origin.
Purple remains assembled after release. Retreat the open right arm along a continuous elbow-up path toward origin, leaving all three pairs clear.
Finish returning the right arm to origin with the gripper open, maintaining elbow-up continuity. All three released matching assemblies remain visually together.
Settle both arms at their initial poses with open grippers and inspect the released assemblies without additional contact.
Purple remains visibly more recessed than blue and yellow. Reapproach for a centered final depth correction rather than assuming the earlier turns completed it.
Bring the open right gripper vertically above purple with clearance, keeping the left arm home and preserving elbow-up continuity.
Lower the open right gripper along the purple nut's observed axis to inspect the grasp center at close range before applying any further turn.
Lower six millimeters to center the purple nut within the finger contact region, then close and hold without twisting so the grasp can be checked.
With purple centered between the fingers, apply a steady clockwise tightening stroke while following downward by only two millimeters. Leave the other assemblies and left arm untouched.

Purple's tip is still recessed despite turning. Test a slow six-millimeter axial follow-through with only a small additional clockwise turn, staying within the current wrist range and monitoring resistance.
Release before resetting the wrist. Raise the open fingers to inspect a higher contact on purple's nut; the lower grasp may be contacting the screw rather than turning the nut effectively.
Purple remains upright and paired after release. Withdraw the open right gripper with clearance and return toward origin rather than continuing to disturb the settled assembly.
Complete the smooth right-arm return to origin with both grippers open, leaving the three released matching assemblies untouched.
